**Comparison and Contrast:**

Both traces solve the same 3-coloring graph problem with identical graph structure. Their approaches diverge in starting heuristic: Trace 1 identifies the triangle A-E-H as its entry point, while Trace 2 starts with the highest-degree node G. Both arrive at valid (different) colorings. Trace 1 explores an alternative solution (C=Green) and then discards it, a grounded branch with visible payoff — this is a CYCLE. Trace 1 also contains extensive repeated edge-by-edge verification (the solver explicitly admits "I am repeating myself because I am paranoid"), which is a clear LOOP. Trace 2 is more linear but re-verifies its solution with a trivial color permutation at the end, adding no new information.

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="So we have a second family of solutions" end="I will stick with the first one I found:" basis="The solver explores an alternative coloring (C=Green, I=Blue), confirms it is valid, then explicitly discards it in favor of the first solution."
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's list the nodes and check all their constraints again." end="I am repeating myself because I am paranoid." basis="The solver re-checks all edges and constraints multiple times, adding no new information, and explicitly admits the repetition."
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="If I swap Blue/Green?" end="This looks just as valid." basis="The solver re-verifies the already-confirmed solution with permuted colors, which is trivially valid for any 3-coloring and adds no new information or constraint."
